title: Sabarmati Weaves adds 12 MW rooftop solar and 20 MWh battery storage across mills
body: Sabarmati Weaves will install 12 MW of rooftop solar and a 20 MWh battery storage system across its four textile mills in Ahmedabad and Kalol, as part of a plan to source 60 per cent of its power from renewables by 2029. The company said the battery storage will be used to shave evening peak demand charges. Sabarmati has invited EPC and equipment bids for string inverters, battery containers and an energy management system, with orders expected before December. The company said peak-hour tariffs have risen sharply in the last two years, and that the storage system should pay back its cost in under six years at current electricity prices.

title: OrbitCore Data Centres signs 50 MW renewable PPA for its second Hyderabad campus
body: OrbitCore Data Centres has signed a 50 MW hybrid solar and wind power purchase agreement for its second data centre campus in Hyderabad, which will have 36 MW of IT load. The company is also planning a battery storage system to replace part of its diesel backup and to manage grid outages. OrbitCore said it will run a tender for a 30 MWh lithium iron phosphate battery storage system with integrated power conversion in the next quarter. The company's first Hyderabad campus is fully leased to two cloud providers, and OrbitCore said the new site is designed to host high-density AI workloads from the first phase.

title: Narmada Vidyut Distribution Company tenders 250 MWh of grid-scale battery storage
body: Narmada Vidyut Distribution Company has issued a tender for 250 MWh of battery energy storage at five substations to manage evening peak demand and absorb surplus daytime solar. The utility will own the systems and wants bidders to supply batteries, power conversion systems and ten years of operations and maintenance. Bids are due on November 5. The distribution company said it plans a second tranche of storage next year if the first projects meet performance targets. The utility said daytime solar output in its area has grown rapidly and that evening peak demand now regularly exceeds available supply, forcing costly short-term power purchases.

title: Marigold Malls & Spaces to put rooftop solar and storage on eleven malls
body: Marigold Malls & Spaces will install 9 MW of rooftop and carport solar across eleven shopping malls and add battery storage at its four largest properties to cut diesel generator use. The programme is part of a green building certification push ahead of a planned real estate investment trust listing. Marigold said it will appoint a single EPC partner and is benchmarking hybrid inverters and commercial battery systems from several manufacturers. Marigold said its malls use about 140 million units of electricity a year, and the solar programme is expected to cut grid consumption by roughly a fifth once all phases are complete.

title: Suryodaya Renewables raises Series B to build 800 MW of solar-plus-storage parks
body: Suryodaya Renewables has raised USD 110 million in a Series B round to build 800 MW of solar parks with co-located battery storage in Rajasthan and Maharashtra. The independent power producer has already signed PPAs with two state utilities and three industrial customers. Suryodaya said it will place orders for central inverters and 400 MWh of battery storage in phases, with the first tranche of equipment orders due in the next six months. The company operates 450 MW of solar capacity today, and said the new projects will supply round-the-clock green power to industrial buyers under long-term contracts.

title: Vistara Auto Components commissions captive solar and plans battery storage at Chennai plants
body: Vistara Auto Components has commissioned a 6 MW captive solar plant at its Oragadam facility and will extend the programme to its two other Chennai plants with a further 8 MW of rooftop solar and 12 MWh of battery storage. The company said customers in Europe are asking for lower-carbon parts. It is tendering for inverters and storage systems that can integrate with its plant SCADA and provide backup during grid outages. Vistara supplies chassis and suspension components to several passenger vehicle makers and said two European customers have set carbon targets for their suppliers from 2028 onwards.

title: Zenith Cloud Infra to build 80 MW data centre campus in Noida with on-site storage
body: Zenith Cloud Infra will build an 80 MW data centre campus in Noida at an investment of INR 7,200 crore, with the first 24 MW hall going live in 2028. The design includes rooftop solar, a 40 MWh battery storage system for grid support and green power sourced through open access. Zenith said it will select battery storage and power conversion suppliers early so that the electrical design can be finalised before construction starts. Zenith said it has already signed a memorandum of understanding with a large cloud provider for the first hall, and that the campus will be powered largely by renewable energy.

title: Annapurna Foods plans 5 MW rooftop solar and storage for its cold storage network
body: Annapurna Foods, a frozen foods and dairy company, will install 5 MW of rooftop solar and 8 MWh of battery storage across seven cold storage warehouses in Punjab and Haryana. The company said electricity is its largest variable cost and the storage will keep refrigeration running through frequent grid outages. Annapurna expects to finalise EPC partners and inverter suppliers by the end of October. Annapurna said its warehouses currently depend on diesel generators for up to four hours a day during summer, which adds significantly to operating costs and emissions.

title: Dakshin Green Energy awarded 300 MW solar-wind hybrid project with storage
body: Dakshin Green Energy has been awarded a 300 MW solar-wind hybrid project with 150 MWh of battery storage in a national auction, with a 25-year PPA at a competitive tariff. The project will be built in Karnataka's Koppal district and must be commissioned within 24 months. Dakshin said it will issue requests for proposals for central inverters, battery containers and a plant controller over the next two months. Dakshin operates about 700 MW of wind and solar capacity across southern India, and said the new project will be its first to include large-scale battery storage.

title: Amrit Steel commits to 100 MW captive solar and storage for new rolling mill
body: Amrit Steel will build 100 MW of captive solar with 60 MWh of battery storage to power a new rolling mill at its Raigarh plant, as part of a INR 2,300 crore capacity expansion. The steelmaker said the storage will smooth solar output for continuous operations. Amrit has begun talks with EPC contractors and plans to sign equipment contracts for inverters, transformers and battery systems in the first quarter of 2027. Amrit Steel produces about 2.5 million tonnes of steel a year and said its customers in construction and automotive are increasingly asking for lower-carbon steel products.

title: Nilachal Tech Parks to add rooftop solar and battery storage across 6 million sq ft
body: Nilachal Tech Parks will install 7 MW of rooftop solar and 10 MWh of battery storage across its 6 million sq ft office portfolio in Bengaluru and Pune. Tenants, including several global technology companies, have asked for renewable power to meet their own climate targets. Nilachal said it will select hybrid inverters and storage systems that support remote monitoring and plans to start installation in January. Nilachal said leasing enquiries for green-certified office space have risen strongly this year, and that the solar and storage programme will help it retain large technology tenants.

title: Sahra Water & Power plans 500 MWh battery storage to support new solar capacity
body: Sahra Water & Power has announced plans for 500 MWh of battery storage across three sites to integrate 1.2 GW of new solar capacity coming online in the next two years. The utility will run a competitive tender for engineering, procurement and construction, including power conversion systems and energy management software. Sahra said pre-qualification opens in October and that it expects to award contracts in the first half of 2027. The utility said the storage projects will help it reduce reliance on gas-fired peaking plants and meet the country's target of generating 30 per cent of power from renewables by 2030.
